sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I could have passed the exam.
I would have done much better on the test.

options.why_wrong: The simple past states a fact that did not happen, so it does not express regret about an unreal past situation.

options.text: I will pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This refers to the future, but the stem expresses regret about the past, so the completion must refer to the past.

options.text: I studied for the exam yesterday.
options.why_wrong: This describes what the speaker actually did, but it does not complete the wish or the imagined result that 'if only' introduces.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.

grammar_focus: Wishes about the past with 'if only' and 'would have' plus past participle
explanation: 'If only' followed by the past perfect expresses regret about a past situation that did not happen, so the main clause uses 'would have' plus the past participle. Ukrainian speakers may use a simple conditional form here, because the first language does not separate the perfect form in the same way.
translation: Якби я тільки більше вчився, я б склав іспит.
